items.title: Perfection of Deportment, Continued: An Erect Body, a Right Aspiration, and Mindfulness Turned Away from the World

items.zh: 端身正願者，云何端身？謂策舉身令其端直。云何正願？謂令其心離諂離詐，調柔正直。由策舉身令端直故，其心不為惛沈睡眠之所纏擾。離諂詐故，其心不為外境散動之所纏擾。
items.en: As for an erect body and right aspiration — what is an erect body? It means bracing and raising the body so that it is upright and straight. What is right aspiration? It means causing the mind to be free of flattery and deceit, gentle, pliant, and upright. Because the body is braced and raised so as to be upright, the mind is not entangled and disturbed by dullness and drowsiness. Because it is free of flattery and deceit, the mind is not entangled and disturbed by distraction towards outer objects.

items.zh: 安住背念者，云何名為安住背念？謂如理作意相應念，名為背念，棄背違逆一切黑品故。又緣定相為境念，名為背念，棄背除遣一切不定地所緣境故。如是名為威儀圓滿。
items.en: As for abiding in mindfulness turned away — what is called abiding in mindfulness turned away? It means mindfulness in accord with sound reasoning attention, called mindfulness turned away, because it turns away from and opposes every category of defiled states. Further, mindfulness that takes the mark of concentration as its object is also called mindfulness turned away, because it turns away from and dispels every object belonging to an unconcentrated state. This is called perfection of deportment.

items.title: Section: Body Seclusion and Mind Seclusion — the Locus of Seclusion Closes

items.zh: 云何遠離圓滿？謂有二種。一、身遠離，二、心遠離。身遠離者，謂不與在家及出家眾共相雜住，獨一無侶，是名身遠離。心遠離者，謂遠離一切染污、無記所有作意，修習一切其性是善能引義利定地作意，及定資糧加行作意，是名心遠離。如是此中，若處所圓滿、若威儀圓滿、若身遠離、若心遠離，總攝為一，說名遠離。
items.en: What is perfection of seclusion? That is, it is of two kinds: first, seclusion of body; second, seclusion of mind. Seclusion of body means not dwelling intermingled with householders and monastics of differing purpose, alone and without such company — this is called seclusion of body. Seclusion of mind means turning away from every defiled and every morally neutral mental engagement, and cultivating every mental engagement whose nature is wholesome, able to bring true benefit, whether an engagement fixed in concentration or an engagement belonging to the provisions and preparatory practice for concentration — this is called seclusion of mind. Thus, herein, perfection of place, perfection of deportment, seclusion of body, and seclusion of mind, gathered together as one, are called seclusion.

items.title: Section: The Locus of One-Pointedness of Mind Opens — What Is Samādhi?

items.zh: 云何心一境性？謂數數隨念同分所緣，流注、無罪適悅相應，令心相續，名三摩地，亦名為善心一境性。
items.en: What is one-pointedness of mind? That is, repeated mindful recollection of an object of the same type, flowing in unbroken continuity, joined with blameless ease — causing the mind to continue uninterrupted — this is called samādhi, also called wholesome one-pointedness of mind.

items.title: Repeated Mindful Recollection, and an Object of the Same Type

items.zh: 何等名為數數隨念？謂於正法聽聞受持，從師獲得教誡教授增上力故，令其定地諸相現前。緣此為境，流注、無罪適悅相應，所有正念隨轉安住。
items.en: What is called repeated mindful recollection? That is, through hearing and upholding the true teaching, and through the empowering influence of the instruction and guidance received from a teacher, the various marks belonging to the stage of concentration are made to appear. Taking these as one's object, flowing in continuity and joined with blameless ease, the whole of right mindfulness continues to abide accordingly.

items.zh: 云何名為同分所緣？謂諸定地所緣境界，非一眾多種種品類，緣此為境，令心正行，說名為定，此即名為同分所緣。問：此所緣境是誰同分，說為同分？答：是所知事相似品類，故名同分。
items.en: What is called an object of the same type? That is, the objects belonging to the stage of concentration are not of a single kind but many various categories; taking one of these as the object and causing the mind to move correctly upon it is called concentration, and this is called an object of the same type. Question: of what is this object "of the same type" — of what is it said to be "same"? Answer: it belongs to a category resembling the very thing to be known — hence it is called "of the same type."

items.title: Section: Flowing Continuity and Blameless Ease — the Five Hindrances in Full

items.zh: 復由彼念，於所緣境無散亂行，無缺無間。無間、殷重加行適悅相應而轉，故名流注適悅相應。又由彼念，於所緣境無有染污，極安隱住，熟道適悅相應而轉，故名無罪適悅相應。
items.en: Further, through that mindfulness, engaging the object of meditation without distraction, without lapse, without interruption, continuing on with earnest, sustained effort joined with ease — this is called flowing continuity joined with ease. Further, through that mindfulness, engaging the object of meditation free of defilement, abiding in the utmost peace, continuing on a well-worn path joined with ease — this is called blameless ease.

items.zh: 是故說言：數數隨念同分所緣，流注、無罪適悅相應，令心相續，名三摩地，亦名為善心一境性。

items.title: Two Kinds of One-Pointedness: Calm-Abiding and Insight

items.zh: 復次，如是心一境性，或是奢摩他品，或是毘鉢舍那品。若於九種心住中心一境性，是名奢摩他品；若於四種慧行中心一境性，是名毘鉢舍那品。
items.en: Further, this one-pointedness of mind is either of the calm-abiding type or of the insight type. If it is one-pointedness of mind within the nine stages of mental abiding, this is called the calm-abiding type. If it is one-pointedness of mind within the four kinds of wisdom-conduct, this is called the insight type.

items.title: Section: The Nine Stages of Mental Abiding Named

items.zh: 云何名為九種心住？謂有苾芻，令心內住、等住、安住、近住、調順、寂靜、最極寂靜、專注一趣，及以等持；如是名為九種心住。
items.en: What is called the nine stages of mental abiding? That is, a monk causes the mind: to abide inwardly, to abide continuously, to abide by patching together, to abide closely, to become tamed, to become pacified, to become thoroughly pacified, to attain single-pointed continuity, and to attain equipoise. These are called the nine stages of mental abiding.

items.title: Inward Abiding: The Minister and the Bowl of Oil

items.zh: 云何內住？謂從外一切所緣境界攝錄其心，繫在於內，令不散亂。此則最初繫縛其心，令住於內，不外散亂，故名內住。
items.en: What is inward abiding? That is, gathering the mind back from every external object and binding it inward, so that it does not become distracted. This is the very first binding of the mind, causing it to abide inwardly and not scatter outward — hence it is called inward abiding.

items.zh: 云何等住？謂即最初所繫縛心，其性麁動，未能令其等住、遍住故。次即於此所緣境界，以相續方便、澄淨方便，挫令微細，遍攝令住，故名等住。
items.en: What is continuous abiding? That is, the mind as first bound is still coarse and agitated by nature, not yet able to abide continuously or pervasively. Next, upon this same object, through the means of sustained continuity and the means of purification, one refines it towards subtlety and gathers it pervasively into abiding — hence it is called continuous abiding.

items.zh: 云何安住？謂若此心雖復如是內住、等住，然由失念於外散亂，復還攝錄安置內境，故名安住。
items.en: What is patched-together abiding? That is, although the mind has thus achieved inward abiding and continuous abiding, still, through a lapse of mindfulness, it strays outward — and is then gathered back once more and settled upon the inner object. Hence it is called patched-together abiding.

items.zh: 云何近住？謂彼先應如是如是親近念住，由此念故，數數作意內住其心，不令此心遠住於外；故名近住。
items.en: What is close abiding? That is, having first drawn close to mindfulness again and again in this way, through that mindfulness one repeatedly directs attention to hold the mind inward, not allowing it to stray far outward. Hence it is called close abiding.

items.title: Section: Taming — the Ten Distracting Marks, and the Boy Who Learned to Think Ahead

items.zh: 云何調順？謂種種相令心散亂，所謂色、聲、香、味、觸相，及貪、瞋、癡、男、女等相故，彼先應取彼諸相為過患想。由如是想增上力故，於彼諸相折挫其心，不令流散，故名調順。
items.en: What is taming? That is, various marks cause the mind to become distracted — namely, the marks of form, sound, smell, taste, and touch, and the marks of craving, hatred, delusion, male, and female. One should therefore first take these marks as objects of the perception of their danger. Through the empowering force of this perception, one curbs the mind with respect to these marks and does not allow it to stray — hence it is called taming.

blocks.text: What concentration actually is, and the first stages of the **nine stages of mental abiding**. These nine stages are the classical map of calm (śamatha) in Indian and Tibetan Buddhism.

"Bracing and raising the body so that it is upright and straight." Right aspiration: "the mind free of flattery and deceit, gentle, pliant, upright". "Mindfulness turned away": turned away from worldly distraction.
Body: "not dwelling intermingled with householders and monastics of differing purpose". Mind: "turning away from every defiled and neutral mental engagement".

"Repeated mindful recollection of an object of the same type, flowing in unbroken continuity, joined with blameless ease: this is called samādhi." Venerable Miào Jìng: "same type" stresses the object; one returns to the same kind of object again and again.
"If it is one-pointedness within the nine stages, it is the calm type; if within the four kinds of wisdom-conduct, the insight type."

A monk causes the mind to abide **inwardly**, **continuously**, **by patching**, **closely**; to be **tamed**, **pacified**, **thoroughly pacified**; to have **single-pointed continuity**; and to attain **equipoise**.

"Gathering the mind back from every external object and binding it inward." Master Cháng Bǎi tells the old story of a minister ordered to carry a bowl brimming with oil through the city without spilling a drop, on pain of death; on the way he passed a famous beauty, yet kept his eyes on the bowl. Such is the focus of this first binding.

The mind first bound is coarse; through continuity it becomes subtler. When it strays through lapse of mindfulness, one patches it back. "Close abiding": repeatedly drawing close to mindfulness, "not allowing it to stray far outward".
The ten distracting marks (form, sound, smell, taste, touch, craving, hatred, delusion, male, female). Seeing their faults, one does not let the mind scatter towards them.

quiz.q: "Right aspiration" means a mind free of flattery and deceit. The note makes it renewing a vow before sitting. How do the masters read it?
options: Miào Jìng: the posture is an outward sign — without inner practice it's deceit; Cháng Bǎi: sitting isn't for show while the mind wanders, deceiving donors
quiz.why: "What is right aspiration? It means causing the mind to be free of flattery and deceit, gentle, pliant, and upright." Venerable Miào Jìng: sitting cross-legged is your outward appearance as a practitioner; if inside you don't practice, that is deceit. Master Cháng Bǎi: sitting is not to show off how hard one works while the mind wanders — that deceives the faithful.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 背 in "mindfulness turned away"?
options: means abandoning — turning from faulty mental activity opposed to the path
quiz.why: "Mindfulness in accord with sound reasoning attention is called mindfulness turned away, because it turns away from and opposes every category of defiled states." Venerable Miào Jìng: 背 means abandoning — abandoning all faulty mental activity opposed to the noble path, the "dark category."

quiz.q: Body seclusion: not dwelling mixed with householders and monastics. The English adds "of differing purpose." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it?
options: don't live with those of different aims or methods — keep distance
quiz.why: "Seclusion of body means not dwelling intermingled with householders and monastics of differing purpose, alone and without such company." Venerable Miào Jìng: those of different aspirations shouldn't live together — people with different views, not practising the same method, should keep their distance. "Of differing purpose" is not in the original but matches the lecture.

quiz.q: One-pointedness is "repeated mindful recollection of an object of the same type." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "repeated recollection" shows?
options: neither torpor nor distraction is heavy, so samādhi comes easily
quiz.why: "What is one-pointedness of mind? That is, repeated mindful recollection of an object of the same type … this is called samādhi." Venerable Miào Jìng: "repeated recollection" shows that torpor is not heavy and distraction not heavy either, so samādhi is easily attained.

quiz.q: Repeated recollection rests on "hearing and upholding the true teaching." Does Venerable Miào Jìng include reading on one's own?
options: yes — one's own reading, without necessarily needing a teacher's explanation
quiz.why: "Through hearing and upholding the true teaching, and through the empowering influence of the instruction received from a teacher, the various marks belonging to concentration are made to appear." Venerable Miào Jìng: "hearing" includes one's own reading — one need not have a spiritual friend explain it.

quiz.q: One-pointedness divides into calm and insight types. Which belongs to insight, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: one-pointedness with the four kinds of wise observation
quiz.why: "If it is one-pointedness within the nine stages, this is the calm-abiding type; if within the four kinds of wisdom-conduct, the insight type." Venerable Miào Jìng: one-pointedness with the four kinds of wise observation is the insight type — it belongs to wisdom.

quiz.q: Inward abiding "gathers the mind back from every external object." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 攝錄?
options: 攝 is grabbing it, 錄 restraining it so it doesn't move
quiz.why: "Gathering the mind back from every external object and binding it inward, so that it does not become distracted." Venerable Miào Jìng: 攝 means grabbing hold of it; 錄 means restraining it so it doesn't move about.
